evidence: r-index lib offers count() and locate_all(); its ri-count/ri-locate CLIs are benchmarks that print nothing. No text-extract API (MONI keeps an SLP internally). DNA/byte text.
No IUPAC/wildcard/class patterns in any member; exact BWT backward search only. MONI keeps only A,C,G,T,N in the reference (paper Sec. 4).
No k-error search on the index. MONI 'extend' = MEM seeds + ksw2 SW extension to SAM; authors: 'not a full-featured aligner'. Approximate = split pattern + user code.
MONI 'mems' (MS + thresholds) gives MEMs of reads vs 10-200 human haplotypes; 611M 100bp reads, 32 thr, 8h31 wall. MEM-vs-index only; no MUM or maximal-repeat-pair mode.
Best member PHONI: streamed matching statistics in one pass, no buffering (1000 chr19 = 60.1 GB text, SLP 80.6 MB). MONI 'ms' and SPUMONI MS/PML also output ms; reference r-index route.
Multi-FASTA pangenome index; SPUMONI '-d' document array (+16% size) labels hits per class for multi-class use. No k-common-substring or document-listing API.
SPUMONI indexes forward+reverse complement of references by default (v2.0.1 adds opt-out; paper: RC included). MONI/PHONI/r-index: no RC handling.
JACM paper proves SA/ISA/LCP and suffix-tree ops in O(log(n/r)); released r-index exposes only LF/count/locate, no tree navigation API (suffix links, LCA, string depth).
Big-BWT '-S' writes SA (5 B/int) and '-L' adds LCP (external-memory EM-SparsePhi, not repeat-aware). LRS, distinct substrings, k-mer stats are user code on those arrays.
MONI: 100 human haplotypes in 20h15 wall, 32 thr (~4 Mbp/s, my estimate); 1000 chr19 (60 GB) in 1.3 h. ropebwt3 paper: pfp-thresholds human100 <51.7 h, grlBWT 8.3 h, ropebwt3 20.5 h.
MONI HG.100 index 29.8 GB (~0.1 B/bp est.; PuffAligner 368 GB) but peak build 206 GB (HG.10: 132 GB); chr19.1000 (60 GB text) peaks at 21 GB. Big-BWT paper: 131 MB RLBWT, no SA samples.
ropebwt3 paper Table 4 (CPU kb/s): MONI SMEM 453 vs ropebwt3 1758 vs Movi 5894 (13x faster). r-index count 750-933 us/pattern (Big-BWT paper, 1-1000 chr19).
MONI built and queried HG.100 (29.8 GB index) and HG.200 (200 human haplotypes, ~0.6 Tbp est.); Big-BWT 10,000 Salmonella (49.4 GB). 1000-human-genome build is only extrapolated.
Big-BWT pipeline passes data via files (.parse/.dict/.ilist) and LCP uses external-memory EM-SparsePhi; queries load the whole index into RAM. MONI/SPUMONI code not checked for mmap.
Big-BWT: '-t 4' cuts run time by roughly a factor two. MONI HG.100 used 32 threads but CPU 26h vs wall 20h15 (~1.3 cores average): far from near-linear.
'moni ms/mems -t N' threads over one index (paper: 32 thr, 611M reads); SPUMONI v1.2.0 'multi-threading in run'. No thread-safety contract or concurrency tests documented.
All members build once from the full text (PFP/BWT/r-index); documented commands (build, ms, mems, extend, run) include no append, insert or delete. ropebwt3 FMR is the dynamic option.
1000 chr19 (~60 GB) -> 131 MB RLBWT; MONI 100 human haplotypes 29.8 GB vs PuffAligner 368 GB; SPUMONI 2 index 0.74 GB vs minimap2 50.9 GB (68x smaller).
r-index/Big-BWT take byte text (Big-BWT: no 0x00-0x02); MONI/SPUMONI keep ACGTN; SPUMONI 2 adds general-text and minimizer-alphabet modes. No dedicated 2-bit DNA path.
Members serialize to files (r-index .ri; MONI .slp/.thrbv.ms/.idx) but formats are undocumented and loaded whole into RAM; no mmap, version field or checksum documented.
C++ (sdsl-lite based) plus Python-driven CLIs (moni, phoni, spumoni); no C ABI or NuGet. Best .NET route is spawning the CLI or a C++/CLI wrapper.
MONI: bioconda badge, Docker Hub, .deb/.sh/.tar.gz release assets, CLI; SPUMONI Docker/Singularity (its README); Big-BWT/r-index source only. No PyPI/NuGet/crates.
Big-BWT '-C' and 'bwtcheck' verify BWT/SA/LCP against divsufsort/LCP9 (documented oracle). MONI repo shows no tests dir or CI; validation otherwise in papers.
OSI licences (MIT r-index/PHONI; GPL-3.0 Big-BWT/MONI/SPUMONI). Newest tag MONI v0.2.2 2024-09-19, SPUMONI v2.0.7 2023-05-25 (>24 mo); Big-BWT commits to 2026-08-29; 1-2 open issues.
Count via 'mem' hit counts; locate via sampled SA ('ssa', 'mem -p', 'sw'); README: 'slow on the locate operation'. 'get' extracts only a whole i-th sequence, no substring access.
No IUPAC/wildcard patterns; NEWS 3.4: ambiguous query bases are converted to 'A' in mem. Alphabet fixed to A,C,G,T,N.
'sw' = revised BWA-SW on the FM-index (mismatches, affine gaps, -e end-to-end); 'hapdiv' counts haplotypes at edit distance 1-5. Heuristic, tens of times slower than SMEM search.
'mem' reports SMEMs of queries vs a collection index (Gagie long-MEM algorithm default since 3.2; --gap/--cov); 100-320 human genomes. No MUM or maximal-repeat-pair mode.
'mem' emits SMEM intervals (start,end,hits) per query = MS anchors; 'suffix' = longest matching suffix; C function rb3_fmd_smem(). No per-position ms[] array output.
Collection index: i-th input at BWT seq 2i (revcomp 2i+1); 'get' by id; SSA maps hits to sequence id/offset (PAF). No document listing/counting or k-common-substring API.
Both strands indexed by default (seq i at 2i, reverse complement at 2i+1; -R opts out); FMD bidirectional index (Li 2012) so one SMEM/sw call covers both strands.
No documented tree API; C header exposes SA-interval struct rb3_sai_t, rb3_fmd_extend (bidirectional extend), rb3_fmi_rank*, rb3_ssa locate. No suffix links, LCA or string depth.
Sub-commands 'kount' (high-occurrence k-mers), 'stat' (run count), 'hapdiv'. No LRS, distinct-substring counts or supermaximal repeats.
human100 (301.6 Gb; ~600 Gbp both strands) in 20.5 h at x22.9 threads (~4.1 Mbp/s); 7.3 Tb bacteria in 25.6 d (~3.3 Mbp/s). grlBWT 8.3 h but needs ~2 TB scratch disk.
Build peak 83.0 GB for 301.6 Gb (0.28 B/bp), 67.3 GB for 7.3 Tb; final BWT 27.6 GB for 14.66T symbols; r-index est. >200 GB, pfp-thresholds peak 788 GB on human100.
Table 4 (CPU kb/s, load excluded): SMEM 1758 short reads, 1696 HiFi vs MONI 453, Movi PML 5894 (3.4x faster), fulgor 2718. README admits locate is slow.
Indexed 7.3 Tb of bacterial assemblies (14.66T BWT symbols, 27.6 GB) and 320 human genomes (963 Gb); 64-bit throughout; largest published scale among compared tools.
Build uses no working disk but holds the B+-tree BWT in RAM (67-170 GB peak); FMD query index can be memory-mapped ('mem -M'). Not semi-external build.
'build -t24/-t32', libsais OpenMP; Table 3 average threads x22.9 (human100), x23.7 (human320), x32.4 (7.3 Tb). No speed-up curve published, so near-linear scaling is unverified.
'mem'/'sw' -t N run kt_for workers over one shared read-only FMD (optionally mmap). No thread-safety contract or concurrency tests documented.
FMR format is dynamic: 'build -i old.fmr' appends sequences and BWTs can be merged. No delete/replace of texts and no per-character online append.
7.3 Tb bacterial genomes -> 27.6 GB run-length BWT (>260x smaller than raw text); 17.6 G runs for 14.6 T symbols; FM-index with SSA 1 per 8192 bp = 17.5 GB.
Paper Sec. 3.1: 'hardcoded for the DNA alphabet' {A,C,G,T,N}; no protein, Unicode or integer alphabets. DNA is run-length coded so no separate 2-bit path.
Documented binary formats: FMR (dynamic) and FMD (static, mmap-able) plus .ssa and .len.gz sidecars. No format version, integrity check or hash documented.
C99 CLI (make; zlib, pthread, OpenMP); headers fm-index.h and rld0.h are not packaged as an API, no shared-library target or C ABI. .NET route = spawn process.
CLI; bioconda 3.10 (linux/osx, x64+arm64) and biocontainers image; GitHub releases v3.0-v3.10; prebuilt indices on Zenodo. No PyPI, NuGet or crates.
Repo has no tests dir and no .github/workflows (404 at tag v3.10); Makefile has an asan switch only. Validation is empirical in the paper (320 human genomes, tool comparisons).
MIT licence (libsais Apache-2.0); v3.10 released 2025-11-25, ten releases since 2024-06; 286 commits; 2 open issues; bioconda tracks releases.
